record.paper_title: Semigroups of rational functions: some problems and conjectures
record.original_question: Let P be a non-special rational function of degree at least two. Associate to P the finite multigraph Γ_P whose vertices represent chosen conjugacy-class representatives inside the equivalence class of P under elementary transformations P = V∘U, P' = U∘V, and whose edges correspond to decompositions linking such representatives. Which finite graphs can occur as Γ_P?

evidence.quote: The graph Γ_P is defined as a multigraph whose vertices are in a one-to-one correspondence with some fixed representatives P_i of conjugacy classes in [P], and whose multiple edges connecting the vertices corresponding to P_i to P_j are in a one-to-one correspondence with solutions of the system P_i = V ∘ U, P_j = U ∘ V in rational functions.
Problem 2.4. Which finite graphs occur as graphs Γ_P for non-special rational functions P?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A rational function is a holomorphic self-map of the Riemann sphere CP^1, identified with an element of C(z). Two rational functions A and B are conjugate if there exists a Möbius transformation μ such that B = μ^{-1} ∘ A ∘ μ. For a rational function A of degree at least two and any decomposition A = U ∘ V with U, V rational of degree at least one, the rational function Ã := V ∘ U is called an elementary transformation of A. Two rational functions A and B are called equivalent, written A ~ B, if there is a finite chain of elementary transformations and conjugacies connecting A to B; the equivalence class of A under ~ is denoted [A]. A rational function P of degree at least two is called special if it is conjugate to z^n, ±T_n (a Chebyshev polynomial), or a Lattès map.

Now fix a non-special rational function P of degree at least two. Let {P_i} be a complete set of representatives of the conjugacy classes contained in [P] (it is known that for P non-special this set is finite). Define a finite multigraph Γ_P as follows:
 • The vertex set of Γ_P is in bijection with the chosen representatives {P_i}.
 • For each ordered pair (i, j), the multiple edges joining the vertex for P_i to the vertex for P_j are in bijection with the solutions (U, V) (in rational functions of degree at least one) of the simultaneous system
       P_i = V ∘ U,    P_j = U ∘ V,
   considered up to the natural equivalence that identifies (U, V) with (μ^{-1} U ν, ν^{-1} V μ) for Möbius μ, ν compatible with the chosen representatives.

Question. Characterize precisely which finite multigraphs Γ can arise as Γ_P for some non-special rational function P of degree at least two.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in Pakovich's work on semigroups of rational functions. Related results by Pakovich (e.g., "Recomposing rational functions") show finiteness of [P] up to conjugacy for non-special P, but no characterization of the resulting multigraphs Γ_P appears in the literature; the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Recomposing rational functions
status_evidence.snippet: For any decomposition A=U∘V, the function Ã=V∘U is an elementary transformation; equivalence classes have only finitely many conjugacy classes when A is non-special.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the underlying finiteness needed to define Γ_P for non-special P, but does not characterize which graphs occur.

status_evidence.title: Fedor Pakovich – Arnold Math. J.
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of the equivalence relation generated by elementary transformations on rational functions.
status_evidence.claim: Provides context on [P] and elementary transformations; the classification of Γ_P is not resolved.
